answer:
In the PCA of the twelve forms of capital computed over the 39 hundred-year bins (Pearson correlation matrix, variables re-standardized; sign convention: the largest |loading| on each PC made positive), the three symbolic-capital components are characterized as follows.

**PC1 (dominant axis, 30.3% of variance):** house size, daggers and hatchets/swords all load **positively and only moderately** — house size (Zhausgr) ≈ +0.23, daggers (ZDolch) ≈ +0.27, hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert) ≈ +0.30. Because the sign of PC1 is arbitrary, the robust statement is that the three symbolic components sit on the **same pole** as copper/gold (ZCU_AU +0.41), hoards/deposits (ZHort +0.34), pottery decoration (Zkeverz +0.38) and monument size (ZMW +0.24), and on the **opposite pole** from pottery form (ZKeform −0.35), amber (−0.24), axes/celts (−0.24) and sickle (−0.15). So PC1 is a wealth/prestige gradient in which the symbolic components co-vary positively with the material-wealth indicators (metals, hoards, decorated pottery, monument size).

**PC2 (19.5% of variance):** the three symbolic components **split**. House size carries a clearly **positive PC2 loading (≈ +0.33)** and is therefore the symbolic component that most defines the second-axis contrast (along with axes/celts +0.47, amber +0.44, monument size +0.39 and pottery form +0.38). In contrast, daggers (≈ +0.07) and hatchets/swords (≈ +0.05) have **near-zero PC2 loadings** — they lie essentially on the PC1 axis and contribute little to the PC2 dispersion. In short: house size is the symbolic capital that loads onto PC2, while daggers and hatchets/swords are PC1-aligned with negligible PC2 contribution.

**Period grouping in the PC1–PC2 plane:** the 39 bins separate largely by period, mainly as a temporal gradient on PC1 — Early Neolithic far negative (mean PC1 ≈ −1.74), Middle Neolithic and SG/Corded-Ware intermediate-negative (≈ −1.4 / −1.1), Late Neolithic and Young Bronze Age intermediate-positive (≈ +0.3 / +1.8), Old Bronze Age far positive (≈ +3.1). PC2 adds a secondary contrast (Middle Neolithic high ≈ +1.8, Young Bronze Age low ≈ −1.1), so periods are not perfectly clustered but follow an ordered neolithic→bronze-age trajectory on PC1.

**Robustness:** re-running the same PCA on the interpolated time series binned to 100 years gives the same loading magnitudes (|PC1| ≈ 0.19–0.30 for the three symbolic variables) and the same PC2 pattern (house size clearly loaded, the other two near zero); only the arbitrary global sign of PC1 flips, so the characterization is stable and not materially changed.

payload.hypothesis: In the hundred-year-binned PCA of the 12 forms of capital (correlation matrix, re-standardized; PC1=30.3%, PC2=19.5%), the symbolic components (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) load positively and moderately on PC1 (+0.23/+0.27/+0.30), sharing the same pole as copper/gold, hoards, pottery decoration and monument size — i.e., they ride the dominant wealth/prestige gradient. Along PC2 they split: house size carries a distinct positive loading (~+0.33) and defines the second-axis contrast, while daggers (~+0.07) and hatchets/swords (~+0.05) have near-zero PC2 loadings and are essentially PC1-aligned. The 39 bins follow an ordered neolithic->bronze-age trajectory on PC1 (EN negative to OBA positive) with a secondary MN-high/YBA-low contrast on PC2. A robustness check on the interpolated time series binned to 100y reproduces the same magnitudes and PC2 pattern (only the arbitrary PC1 sign flips).
payload.workflow: Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal=','; 39 rows, BCE 500-4300 step 100, 0 NAs), dropped group/color, took the 12 Z-capital variables, re-standardized (mean 0, unit variance), computed the Pearson correlation matrix, performed eigendecomposition (numpy.linalg.eigh), sorted by eigenvalue, fixed each PC sign so the largest-|loading| is positive, and read off PC1/PC2 loadings and period-grouped scores. Robustness: binned data/time_series_data.csv *_inter columns to 100y by BCE=-CE (groupby mean) and repeated the same PCA.
